transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Silverline CTO), Ethan Cole (Backend Eng), Maya Singh (Product)

Summary: quick discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Silverline evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Interested in time-to-first-token, free credits, trial experience. Security and data residency questions flagged.

Topics: quickstart, free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem), SOC2/KMS, model variants, latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot scope

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with me is Lena our solutions engineer. Thanks for taking the time
[00:10] Priya (Silverline CTO): thanks, Jordan. we are short on time but excited to hear the quickstart details, we want something the product team can ship against quickly
[00:18] Jordan: awesome. quick context — silverline is looking at adding LLM features to search and triage workflows? is that right priya?
[00:24] Priya: yeah, primarily two projects — smart search snippets and an internal triage assistant for support. timeline is Q3 pilot, production later this year pending cost and compliance.
[00:36] Lena (Redwood SE): to set expectations, our PLG quickstart is designed to get you to first-token in minutes: API keys, SDK snippets, pre-approved model profiles. you also get a small pool of free credits for evaluation and sample prompts.
[00:52] Ethan (Silverline): what's the typical free credits amount? and does it include streaming?
[00:58] Jordan: generally we give a $500 credit for initial self-serve sign-ups for teams (varies by program). streaming is supported out of the box — you'll see both streaming and non-streaming examples in the quickstart.
[01:12] Maya (Product): do we need to spin up anything on our side for the quickstart or is it pure API?
[01:18] Lena: it's pure API for hosted. the flow is sign up, get API key, run sample calls. for Dedicated or Private we have extra steps — Dedicated is reserved capacity with dedicated GPU pools, Private involves VPC or on-prem deployment and our private control plane. but you don't need Dedicated to run the quickstart.
[01:36] Priya: ok. our compliance team will ask about SOC2 and encryption. do you have audits and KMS support?
[01:43] Jordan: yes — SOC 2 Type II, support for customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated. hosted also supports encryption at rest, but if you need customer-managed keys that's part of the Private offering. we'll send the security pack.
[01:58] Priya: noted. and data residency? we have EU customers, need data not to leave region for some features.
[02:06] Lena: we have region-aware routing and a private deployment option for strict residency. Hosted can be region pinned depending on rollout — we'll capture requirements and confirm options.
[02:18] Ethan: on the technical side, latency is a big one — sub-200ms for short chat turn is ideal for us. can the hosted API hit that?
[02:27] Lena: it depends on model and sequence length. for smaller open models we've seen median latency under 150ms for single-turn generation on our hosted infra; for heavier models it expands. Dedicated gives you more predictable p99s because of reserved GPU pools. we can propose a benchmark during the pilot.
[02:45] Priya: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private again — I need to explain to execs.
[02:51] Jordan: Dedicated = reserved capacity in Redwood-managed infra, isolated GPU pools, SLA-backed. Private = your VPC or on-prem where the control plane is private; more work to set up but gives you full network isolation and customer key control.
[03:07] Maya: any differences in SDK or API surface?
[03:10] Lena: no — we keep the API consistent across modes so devs can switch without app changes. config flags for routing and model pinning handle the infra differences.
[03:19] Speaker 1: (mumble) question on pricing — how does the unit cost compare hosted vs dedicated?
[03:24] Jordan: hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated has committed monthly/annual pricing with lower unit costs at scale. Redwood Optimize recommendations can also shrink costs via batching, quantization profiles, and caching.
[03:36] Ethan: we already run some in-house models on EC2 and a small KF infra. one of our concerns is falling back to open-source models if capacity tight — is that supported?
[03:47] Lena: yes, routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants, including quantized open models. note that quality varies so we'll set rollout rules and can do A/B tests in the console.
[04:00] Priya: security follow-up: do you provide audit logs per user and per-route? our auditors demand that.
[04:06] Jordan: yes, per-token/log-level audit trails, RBAC and SAML/SSO integrations for access control. we'll attach the audit log export examples in the doc pack.
[04:20] Maya: how long does it usually take for a team to go from sign-up to a live simple integration?
[04:26] Lena: for the PLG quickstart, many teams get a prototype in a day and production in weeks. the time-to-first-token is literally minutes once you have the API key and sample prompt.
[04:36] Priya: good. what are the common gotchas?
[04:39] Jordan: throttles and rate limits if you blast parallel requests; prompt latency when you don't batch effectively; and compliance gating if you need Private/VPC. also proper key management and monitoring — we recommend starting with small quotas.
[04:54] Ethan: we want to test latency and cost at scale. can you provide a benchmark harness we can run?
[04:59] Lena: yes, we'll share a lightweight benchmark repo that hits typical prompt shapes and sequence lengths. we'll include the KV cache/prefix caching set ups — sometimes transcribed as KV cash or K V cache in notes (ha).
[05:12] Priya: will you give us an estimate for pilot cost?
[05:14] Jordan: we'll propose a small pilot with a few thousand dollars in credits for the eval and then estimate production cost based on throughput and model choices.
[05:24] Maya: on the compliance front — can you support SSO for our internal teams?
[05:28] Jordan: yes, SAML/Sso and SCIM for provisioning.
[05:31] Speaker 2 (Ethan): a quick tech nit — does Redwood support token-level cost breakdown in logs?
[05:36] Lena: yes, token-level cost and latency metrics per route in the console. helps optimize prompt engineering and batching.
[05:45] Priya: ok let's recap next steps before we run out.
[05:48] Jordan: sure. recap: Jordan to send quickstart guide, details on free credits, and SOC2/security pack. Lena to send benchmark repo and proposed latency/cost tests. Priya to share infra diagram and compliance checklist. we'll schedule a deeper 60-min technical demo/benchmark session week of 2026-04-27.
[06:10] Priya: sounds good. can you also include a sample canary rollout plan for model upgrades?
[06:14] Lena: yes, small canary, A/B, automatic fallback; will include in doc set.
[06:20] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email and send calendar invite for the demo.
[06:24] Maya: thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: minor transcription mis-hearings (product names like KV cache appear as 'K V cash' or 'K V cache'), occasional speaker attribution errors (Speaker 1). Natural speech patterns preserved, some filler words.

References shared: Quickstart guide link: https://app.redwood.ai/quickstart (sent post-call); Benchmark repo (to be shared by Lena); Security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (sample link)

End of transcript.
